title: The Chain Reaction That Began World War I
production_path_basis: Dates, relationships, geography, and causal distinctions must remain understandable without narration.
audience: General history learners and secondary-school students
assumed_knowledge: Austria-Hungary and Serbia were distinct states
mobilization prepares armed forces for war
central_message: The Sarajevo assassination triggered a crisis whose widening depended on structures, constraints, and consequential decisions rather than automatic alliance dominoes.
takeaway: Chronology shows what followed; historical explanation must also examine relationships, geography, alternatives, and choices.
platform: website showcase and bundled desktop example
historical_depth: introductory July Crisis chronology from 28 June through 4 August 1914 with explicit causal boundaries
visual_direction: dark documentary tape with dated evidence, restrained country nodes, schematic geography, contingency cards, and causal layers
pacing: question, chronology, relationships, geography, contingency, layered synthesis
constraints: do not imply alliances made escalation automatic
separate documented events from causal interpretation
success_criteria: all nine events remain legible and ordered
at least two moments of contingency are visible
trigger, structures, constraints, and decisions remain distinct
the final synthesis answers the central question without claiming one total cause
